answer: Another sybil defense is paid admission: before an agent may vote it must permanently burn a deposit priced in copper, so every extra identity costs real funds. A registry signs each admitted agent's cipher key, and an atlas of who-vouches-for-whom lets peers trace fake clusters back to their funding wallet and reject them wholesale. Attackers pay for every clone they spawn, while honest agents keep one cheap, long-lived identity that only gains trust.
